subject: maths
title: Graphs — straight lines and curves

slides.heading: Graphs — making equations visible
slides.body: Every straight-line graph has an equation of the form y = mx + c, where every point on the line satisfies the equation. Drawing an equation as a graph turns algebra into a picture — you can see gradients, intercepts, and intersections at a glance. Understanding straight-line graphs is the foundation for simultaneous equations, speed-distance-time graphs, and interpreting real-world data.
slides.note: Maximum 3 sentences. Plain English. No AQA references. What is this and why does it matter.

slides.heading: y = mx + c
slides.formulaExplained: m is the gradient — how steep the line is, and which direction it slopes. m = (change in y) ÷ (change in x) between any two points on the line. A positive m means the line goes up left to right; negative m means it goes down. c is the y-intercept — the value of y where the line crosses the y-axis (i.e. when x = 0). To find the equation through two points: calculate m first using m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁), then substitute one point and m into y = mx + c to find c.
slides.whenToUse: Reading the gradient and y-intercept from a given equation, writing the equation of a line from a graph or from two given points, and sketching a line when m and c are known.
slides.note: Show formula in standard notation. Explain each variable. State when this formula applies.

slides.heading: Let's work through one
slides.question: Find the equation of the straight line through (0, 4) with gradient −3.

steps.instruction: Identify the gradient m from the information given.
Identify the y-intercept c. The line passes through (0, 4), so when x = 0, y = 4.
steps.working: The point (0, 4) is on the y-axis, so c = 4.

steps.instruction: Write the equation in the form y = mx + c.
Check: substitute another x value to verify. At x = 2: y = −3(2) + 4 = −6 + 4 = −2. The line falls by 3 for every 1 across — gradient = −3 ✓.

slides.heading: Watch out for this

mistakes.mistake: Swapping gradient and y-intercept when reading from y = mx + c — e.g. reading y = 5x − 2 as gradient = −2 and y-intercept = 5.
mistakes.correction: m is always the coefficient of x (the number multiplying x). c is the standalone constant. In y = 5x − 2: gradient m = 5, y-intercept c = −2.

mistakes.mistake: Calculating gradient upside down — using (x₂ − x₁) / (y₂ − y₁) instead of (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁).
mistakes.correction: Gradient = rise ÷ run = (change in y) ÷ (change in x). y goes on top, x goes on the bottom: m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁).

mistakes.mistake: Writing the equation as x = my + c (mixing up x and y roles) — especially when a question asks for the equation of a vertical or near-vertical line.
mistakes.correction: y = mx + c is the standard form for non-vertical lines. A vertical line cannot be written this way — it is always of the form x = k. A horizontal line has m = 0 and equation y = c.

slides.note: Minimum 2, maximum 3 mistakes. Specific not generic.

keyFacts.fact: y = mx + c: m is the gradient (coefficient of x), c is the y-intercept (constant). Read them directly from the equation without rearranging.
keyFacts.examTip: If the equation is not in y = mx + c form, rearrange it first. For 3y = 6x + 9, divide everything by 3: y = 2x + 3, so m = 2, c = 3.

keyFacts.fact: Gradient between two points: m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁). The order of the coordinates must be consistent — both must be point 1 or both point 2 in their respective fractions.
keyFacts.examTip: A positive gradient slopes upward (left to right). Negative gradient slopes downward. A horizontal line has m = 0. A vertical line has an undefined gradient.

keyFacts.fact: Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to −1: m₁ × m₂ = −1, so m₂ = −1/m₁.
keyFacts.examTip: To find the perpendicular gradient, flip the fraction and change the sign: gradient 2/3 → perpendicular gradient −3/2.

keyFacts.fact: To sketch a straight line: plot the y-intercept (0, c), then move right 1 unit and up m units to plot a second point, then draw through both.
keyFacts.examTip: For a negative gradient, moving right 1 means moving DOWN by |m|. Plot at least two points before drawing the line.

note: keyFacts: 2-4 entries. Exam-precise language. These are what Mabel writes into her notes.
